jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in South Carolina, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in South Carolina, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county, South Carolina Senate, South Carolina House and U.S. House districts, cities and towns, school districts and ZIP codes.
jsonld.keywords: South Carolina district map, what district am I in, South Carolina Senate district, South Carolina House district, South Carolina congressional district, South Carolina school district lookup

brand.tagline: Every civic district that covers your point in South Carolina, and who represents you there.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 7 congressional districts — the largest districts South Carolina carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 7 features for South Carolina, measured 2026-10-10. South Carolina did not redraw for 2026: the 120th-Congress map and the 119th's (layer 4) carry the same seven districts, every one differing by under 0.001% of its area.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: South Carolina Senate District
layers.rank_note: 46 Senate districts — the same count as the state's counties, and drawn independently of them

source.answers: The South Carolina Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 46 features, measured 2026-10-10. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 20 m interval and refused over a 25 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: sc-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the South Carolina General Assembly's own Senate member pages (name, party, State House office, business telephone and the member's own page). The General Assembly publishes no e-mail addresses, only a message form on each member's page, so none is carried.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 46 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 46 features, measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: None yet — identity only. Every South Carolina county is governed by an elected county council; the state Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office publishes every council district and the State Election Commission's results name the winners, and neither is wired in this first change. Recorded as gap sc-county-council.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 72 unified (K-12) districts covering the whole state, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file)

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), queried live at runtime; 72 features for South Carolina, measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY. South Carolina's school boards are not all chosen the same way, and no statewide roster of their members has been established here — recorded as gap sc-school-board-members.
source.applies: South Carolina — statewide. The label carries no qualifier because there is nothing to distinguish it from: the elementary and secondary tilings TIGERweb serves for other states are EMPTY in South Carolina (0 features each, measured 2026-10-10), and the 72 unified districts' Census land area sums to exactly the 46-county total (77,866 km2).

layers.label: South Carolina House District
layers.rank_note: 124 House districts — the smallest of the three chamber tilings

source.answers: The South Carolina House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (state lower chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 124 features, measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: sc-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the South Carolina General Assembly's own House member pages.

layers.label: Judicial Circuit
layers.rank_note: 16 judicial circuits of whole counties, 5,185 km2 mean area, measured 2026-10-16 on the drawn file — larger on average than a State Senate district (1,804 km2), smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The judicial circuit covering the point: the circuit court there, how many judges the General Assembly elects for it, and the solicitor its voters elect.

boundary.label: Dissolved from the shipped county fabric (TIGERweb State_County layer 1) by sc/scripts/build_sc_judicial_circuits.py, following the county lists in S.C. Code Section 14-5-610 as the Legislature publishes it (read 2026-10-16).
S.C. Code Section 1-7-310 — one solicitor for each circuit, elected by its voters for four years
Constitution of South Carolina, Article V — circuit judges elected by the General Assembly for six years (section 13) and rotated around the state (section 14)

source.people: No judge or solicitor is named yet, because no list of them by circuit has been read; recorded as gap sc-judicial-circuit-officers. The card gives the number of judges the statute sets for the circuit and says the General Assembly, not the voters, elects them.

layers.label: Census County Division
layers.rank_note: 299 census county divisions, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file) — median 226.5 km2 of land (mean 260.4), measured 2026-10-15: smaller than a state House district (median 282.5 km2), larger than a county council district (median 172.0 km2)

source.answers: The census county division containing the point, and its county.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 1 (county subdivisions), queried live at runtime (no builder script, no committed data/app file); 299 features for South Carolina, every one a census county division (LSADC 22, FUNCSTAT S), measured 2026-10-15.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER. A census county division is an area the Census Bureau draws to report its counts: no one is elected from it, and South Carolina has no township governments, so the county governs everyone outside a city or town. The card names the division and its county and says it governs nobody.

layers.label: County Council District
layers.rank_note: 315 council districts in 46 counties (one of them, Hampton's, the whole county) — smaller than a state House district and larger than most ZIP codes

source.answers: The county council district covering the point, the council member(s) it elects, and the members elected by the whole county.

boundary.label: South Carolina Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office — County Council Districts, all 46 counties in one layer, pre-built and shipped with the app; 315 features, measured 2026-10-11. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 20 m interval and refused over a 25 m fidelity ceiling, with every county's districts held to cover that county.

source.people: sc-county-council-members.json, built from the South Carolina Election Commission's certified results and checked weekly by CI: each seat's most recent general election winner (2022 or 2024), dated, with party. A winner is not a claim about who sits today, and the card says so. Each county's own council page is read beside the results, and where it names someone else, calls a seat vacant, leaves the winner off or lists the winner as a former member (eleven seats on 2026-10-11) the card prints both.
source.applies: South Carolina — all 46 counties. Hampton elects its whole council at large and Jasper elects its council by the whole county from four residence townships, so both cards name every member.

layers.label: School Board District
layers.rank_note: 383 districts on the boards of 54 school districts, pre-built from the Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office's layer — 195.4 km2 mean area (median 128.5), measured 2026-10-16 on the drawn file: smaller than a county council district (median 172.0 km2), larger than most ZIP codes

source.answers: The district a school board elects a member from, the school district whose board it is, how many members the district elects, and who votes for them, as the board's own act of the General Assembly says: the district's voters, every voter in the school district, or not stated.

boundary.label: South Carolina Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office — "School Board Districts", layer 0 of the Boundaries_Districts service on gis.state.sc.us: 383 districts on the boards of 54 school districts and one record marked “At Large” for each of the other 18, measured 2026-10-16, pre-built by sc/scripts/build_sc_school_board_districts.py and shipped with the app. The service states no licence, only an as-is disclaimer.

South Carolina General Assembly — each board's own act, read in its ratified text on 2026-10-16 (for example Act 230 of 2024, which sets the Aiken County board), for how many members each district elects and who votes for them; the builder lists all 54

source.people: NO NAMES YET. No statewide list of South Carolina's school board members has been read — the School Boards Association sends its directory on request, and the State Election Commission's results site answers GitHub's servers with no page — so the card names no one rather than guessing, and links the school district's own website; recorded as gap sc-school-board-members.
source.applies: The 54 South Carolina school districts whose boards are elected from districts. The other 18 are marked “At Large” on the state's map and have no districts to draw; the empty card says so.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 841 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas in the state's own bounding box, fetched live by envelope; the layer hides outside South Carolina

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, queried live at runtime. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='45'. 841 features in South Carolina's box, measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: South Carolina. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code (the Georgia test point gives 30817).

layers.label: Voting Precinct
layers.rank_note: 2,315 precincts tiling the state, pre-built from the Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office's official maps — 35.84 km2 mean area, land and water (median 12.82), measured 2026-10-15 on the drawn file: smaller on average than a census county division (260.4 km2 of land), larger than a city or town (18.58)

source.answers: The voting precinct containing the point — where a reader votes and how their ballots are reported.

boundary.label: South Carolina Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office — Voter Precincts, the official maps of the precinct lines the General Assembly sets by act (S.C. Code Title 7, Chapter 7); 2,315 features, pre-built for the state by sc/scripts/build_sc_precincts.py and shipped with the app. Each record names the act that set its lines and the date they took effect, which the card prints, and the county's voter registration and elections office, which the card links. No licence is named, only an as-is disclaimer.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, and none is missing. A precinct elects nobody — it is an election-administration unit, not a district with a representative — so the card says that rather than leaving a reader to wonder which name is absent.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 271 incorporated cities and towns, live from TIGERweb

source.answers: The city or town containing the point, if any.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), queried live at runtime; 271 features for South Carolina (69 cities, 202 towns), measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. South Carolina's cities and towns elect councils, and no statewide roster was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap sc-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: South Carolina — statewide. A point outside every city and town is unincorporated, which the card states.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-10-10: 432 points in South Carolina's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: South Carolina — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in Georgia or North Carolina, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

layers.label: Tribal Government
layers.rank_note: Tribal land — South Carolina has 2 pieces held by one nation, the Catawba Reservation (4.123 km²) and its off-reservation trust land (0.054 km²), both in York County near Rock Hill, MEASURED by scripts/build_tribal_areas.py. Drawn below municipalities, since the reservation is smaller than the city of Rock Hill beside it, and above the point layers. Drawn although no district is drawn on this land, by Adam's ruling of 2026-09-30: a government answers for that ground, so a reader who clicks it should be told which one.

source.answers: Whether this address is on tribal land, and which nation's government answers for it — South Carolina has 2 such areas, both the Catawba Indian Nation's.

boundary.label: US Census Bureau TIGERweb AIANNHA, current vintage — federal reservations and off-reservation trust land, shipped with the app

source.people: The Catawba Nation's Executive Committee, from the nation's own page at catawba.com, read weekly by scripts/tribal_council_scraper.py and dated on the card. The government, its seat and its website come from the Bureau of Indian Affairs' tribal leaders directory (data/bia-tribal-governments.json); the land is joined to the government by this project's own data/tribal-government-join.json.
source.applies: South Carolina — the Catawba Reservation and its trust land in York County, east of Rock Hill. Every other point in the state is on no tribal land.

anchor_point.note: the State House, Columbia, Richland County

negative_point.note: Wilkes County, GEORGIA, about 25 km west of the Savannah River — outside South Carolina and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-10: TIGERweb's state layer names Georgia at this point (control: the State House anchor returns South Carolina). GEORGIA BECAUSE NO INSTANCE SERVES IT, and on land well clear of the river, whose channel the county fabric could place on either side.

geometry.note: The whole-South Carolina outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the 46-county fabric.
The 46 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 7 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120).
The 315 county council districts in all 46 counties, from the state Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office (sc/scripts/build_sc_county_council_districts.py).

South Carolina's tribal land (scripts/build_tribal_areas.py) — the Catawba Reservation and its off-reservation trust land. The floor and the ceiling are equal because that is what the Census publishes inside the state on the current vintage, measured 2026-10-12; a change in either direction is a change in the Census's own map and wants reading rather than a widened bound.

Every South Carolina voting precinct, pre-built by sc/scripts/build_sc_precincts.py through scripts/statewide_precincts.py from the Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office's layer (Douglas-Peucker at 8 m, the smallest of 4, 8 and 12 m that keeps the file at or under 2.5 MB gzipped; a 6,000-point agreement gate, measured 99.97% with zero overlaps; an exact 2,315 count on the fetch and the drawn file). 7.8 MB, 2.24 MB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

Every South Carolina school board district, pre-built by sc/scripts/build_sc_school_board_districts.py through scripts/published_district_layers.py from the Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office's layer (Douglas-Peucker at 4 m; a 400-point agreement gate on every board's extent, measured 99.99% with zero overlaps; an exact 383 count, after the 18 records marked “At Large” are skipped). 4.6 MB, 1.43 MB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.
The 16 judicial circuits of S.C. Code Section 14-5-610, dissolved from the county fabric by sc/scripts/build_sc_judicial_circuits.py, each carrying the number of judges the section sets for it.

rosters.note: U.S. House (SC) roster, refreshed weekly by update-sc-congress-roster.yml.
South Carolina Senate roster from the General Assembly's own member pages, refreshed weekly. The floor is below 46 because a vacant seat is a real event; the chamber listed all 46 on 2026-10-10.
South Carolina House roster from the General Assembly's own member pages, refreshed weekly. The floor is below 124 for the same reason; the chamber listed all 124 on 2026-10-10.
County council members, one key per county FIPS, from the Election Commission's certified results, refreshed weekly by update-sc-county-council-roster.yml.
The recorded gaps this instance ships with, rendered by the data-gaps panel.

The Catawba Nation's Executive Committee, keyed by the Census AIANNH code of its land — scripts/build_tribal_areas.py --rosters from data/tribal-councils.json, which scripts/tribal_council_scraper.py re-reads weekly (update-tribal-councils.yml, listed in the Wisconsin worksheet because one root workflow belongs to one instance). Merged onto tribal-areas.json by the layer's loader, so the land stays cache-first and the names network-first.
